questions.q: In the lab scenario, what phrase in the change manager's requirement signals that a UI Policy alone is insufficient?
options: "a 'Change Reason' field"
"even for changes created automatically through our REST API integration"
"whenever Risk is set to 'High'"
"mandatory on every Change Request"
questions.explain: That phrase states the rule must hold true outside the form — the exact signal that rules out a UI Policy, which only governs the browser form.

questions.q: Why specifically does a UI Policy fail to enforce the requirement for records created by the vendor's REST API integration?
options: UI Policies are deprecated in current ServiceNow releases
The integration's write never renders the Change Request form, so the UI Policy's condition and action never evaluate
The Change Request table doesn't support UI Policies
UI Policies only apply to Incident, never Change Request
questions.explain: A UI Policy only fires when its governed form actually renders in a browser; a direct API write never does that, so the rule is silently skipped.

questions.q: In the Data Policy built for this scenario, what are the Table, Condition, and Rule set to?
options: Table: Incident; Condition: Priority is 1; Rule: Asset Tag mandatory
Table: Change Request; Condition: Risk is High; Rule: Change Reason mandatory
Table: Change Request; Condition: State is Closed; Rule: Change Reason read-only
Table: sys_user; Condition: Active is true; Rule: Email mandatory
questions.explain: The Data Policy governs Change Request, applies when Risk is High, and sets Change Reason mandatory — matching the requirement exactly.

questions.q: Why is it safe, and beneficial, to turn on Apply to UI in this scenario?
options: It removes the server-side enforcement, which is preferred here
It has no effect of any kind and can be ignored
It replaces the Data Policy with a UI Policy automatically
It gives the human-facing form live mandatory feedback while the server-side enforcement still holds regardless of that setting
questions.explain: Apply to UI only adds a form-level mirror of the rule; it never weakens or removes the Data Policy's server-side enforcement.

questions.q: What is the single most important property of a correctly configured Data Policy, as demonstrated in this lab?
options: It only works on tables with fewer than 10 fields
It is write-path-agnostic: the rule holds true regardless of whether the record came from a form, an API, an import, or a script
It must always be paired with a Business Rule to function
It can only be configured by a developer, never an administrator
questions.explain: That write-path-agnostic enforcement is exactly why a Data Policy, not a UI Policy, was the correct tool for this requirement.
